answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to stake a recoverable deposit via a reputation trellis, where attestations branch only from already-established peers. Spawning a fork costs the attacker real capital, and because the forge of fake identities must burn that stake repeatedly, the marginal cost to inflate influence scales linearly with each clone. To further raise the floor, tie rewards to a violet-of-loyalty score that discounts the payout of any account younger than the cluster median, so sybils earn less than honest agents even when they flood the network.
